scope: Canonical Windows input ownership and independent guardian execution against controlled Win32 API boundaries on Linux. No native Windows or task/E2E claim.
contracts: A scan-code acknowledgement owns the scan plus extended flag, not another key with the same low byte or the opposite modifier side.
A virtual-key fallback acknowledgement owns its exact VK and the left-side report of a generic modifier. A zero scan code is not shared ownership.
Missing held-key thread/layout observation fails closed.
Successfully released key/Unicode guardian acknowledgements are retired. Later EOF retries only previously failed pending entries under the existing recovery policy.

guardian_component.method: Actual _guardian_main pipe-reader/queue/recovery loop with a stateful controlled send boundary. After deadline release, another owner reacquires successful entries before EOF; known refused entries remain pending.

KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE and KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY are distinct flags on acknowledged keyboard input.

limits: GetAsyncKeyState does not distinguish two physical keys sharing one virtual key, such as main and keypad Enter, or prove physical-device provenance.
A later parent ownership update is a separate protocol event; this component proves successful deadline recovery followed by EOF without a new acquisition update.
No latency, goodput, coverage, automatic application-context discovery or operation readiness is inferred.
No native Windows verification: current process is Linux and Win32 boundaries are controlled.
